messages:
maria-cs: FYI — BrightCart reported a change in product price extraction after yesterday's rollout. They say the model started inserting '(approx)' in prices it used to return exactly. Customer provided two failing examples.

jason-eng: Thanks, can you paste one of the original prompts + the model response (redact user PII)? we need the exact input/response pair and the model id/variant they hit. Also which environment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

maria-cs: Hosted. Model: redwood/longform-v1 -> we rolled v2.3 yesterday. Example prompt (redacted):

```
SYSTEM: You are an assistant that extracts pricing from merchant descriptions.
USER: Product: "3-pack socks" price info: "Now $9.99, save 20%". Return only price (USD)
```

Customer's response from model (current): "$9.99 (approx)"
Previous expected: "$9.99"

elaine-ml: Interesting — looks like a behavior change where the model sometimes hedges numeric outputs. Need the request-level metadata: temperature, top_p, any system prompt changes, and the prompt logs (the raw request payloads). If you can export the request id(s) we can correlate with serving traces.

maria-cs: I asked BrightCart to export logs — they gave us two request IDs: req_01G8A2... and req_01G8A3... (they said ok to share).

jason-eng: Great. @ryan-oncall can you pull the inference logs for those request ids and check if KV caching or fallback to a safety-ish model happened? also check if the rollout percentage changed around that time.

ryan-oncall: pulling now. Deploy bot shows rollout event at 2026-03-12T22:10Z: redwood/longform-v1 -> v2.3 gradual rollout started 22:10, traffic 30% -> 60% over 2h. I'll check kernel selection and quantization path for those request timestamps.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout redwood/longform-v2.3 started by @elaine-ml — id: rollout-20260312-2230 — target: 60% traffic 

elaine-ml: Two quick asks to speed repro: 1) please ask BrightCart to run a minimal repro with exactly the same headers/params: model=redwood/longform-v2.3, temperature=0.0, max_tokens=16, top_p=1.0, and include the system prompt above. 2) If they can attach the exact curl/python call they used that produced the '(approx)' output, include it.

maria-cs: I sent instructions and a small repro template to BrightCart. Template includes this curl — asked them to copy/paste and run: 

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/longform-v2.3","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that extracts pricing from merchant descriptions."},{"role":"user","content":"Product: \"3-pack socks\" price info: \"Now $9.99, save 20%\". Return only price (USD)"}],"temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":16}'
```

maria-cs: I've also asked them to upload the raw request JSON (safe to redact auth) and confirm whether they were using the route param `&fallback=enabled` or any custom routing.

jason-eng: While we wait, two mitigations we can offer BrightCart: 1) pin to previous version (redwood/longform-v1) via the Console -> Model Pinning UI or by passing model=redwood/longform-v1 in the request. 2) Add a simple post-processing rule that strips parenthetical qualifiers (quick temporary fix). Which do they prefer?

maria-cs: They asked for pinning first. I set a 24h pin for their account to v1, low-friction.

elaine-ml: Good. Once we have the exact repro I'll run a targeted eval on identical prompts and do a diff on token-level logits if needed. If the hedging is a new safety/regression heuristic in v2.3 we might see an anchor token inserted at generation start.

ryan-oncall: pulled traces — for req_01G8A2 the request did hit v2.3 and kernel: int8-merged was selected. There was no fallback. Latency normal. I attached (redacted) inference trace chunk: `logit_bias` not set, sequence start tokens show a token for '(' at position 3 in some examples — could be a decoding prefix.

jason-eng: Thanks. That points at either a decoding/config change or a subtle prompt-conditioning change. Elaine — if you want, we can ask SRE to run a small A/B with v1 vs v2.3 on the same traffic for a focused dataset.

elaine-ml: Yes please. @ryan-oncall coordinate a short A/B eval on 200 example prompts (we can reuse BrightCart's sample set). Keep temperature=0 and deterministic sampling. I'll prepare a diff script.

maria-cs: BrightCart ran the curl repro and confirmed the output is "$9.99 (approx)" consistently with v2.3. They sent the raw JSON for two requests (redacted auth). Uploaded to the support ticket.

jason-eng: Perfect. Next steps: 1) A/B run + logits diff (elaine). 2) If we see an introduced token bias, prepare a hotfix to disable that heuristic or adjust decoding defaults. 3) Keep the pin on v1 until fix validated.

maria-cs: I'll update BrightCart with current mitigation and ETA for follow-up. :thumbsup:

ryan-oncall: started the A/B job. Job id ab-20260313-001 — will post results here when ready.

elaine-ml: thanks everyone — please paste any extra customer examples in this thread; short ones are most valuable.

maria-cs: will do, closing loop with customer now and will drop any other examples here.
